starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends

## Key terms

{{< glossary proposition truth-value boolean-variable logical-operator negation conjunction disjunction exclusive-or implication compound-proposition operator-precedence >}}

## 16.1 Propositions: true or false

- A **proposition** is a statement that is **true** or **false**.
- We name them p, q, r. In code: a `bool` (`hasKey`, `hasTorch`).
- "3 > 5" is a proposition (false). "Open the door!" and "Is the boss
  alive?" are not.

![Propositions or not?](images/propositions.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"health > 50" is true or false only when health has a value.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find the propositions"}
Write three propositions about a racing game and one sentence that is not
a proposition.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Propositions"}
Is it a proposition? Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="yes, it is true|yes, it is an order"}
"The player has the key."
:   yes, it is true or false

"Open the door!"
:   no, it is an order

"3 > 5"
:   yes, it is false

"Is the boss alive?"
:   no, it is a question
:::
:::

## 16.2 NOT, AND and OR

- **¬p** (NOT, `!p`): true when p is false.
- **p ∧ q** (AND, `p && q`): true only when **both** are true.
- **p ∨ q** (OR, `p || q`): true when **at least one** is true.
- Key (T), no torch (F): iron door p ∧ q = F; wooden door p ∨ q = T; trap
  ¬q = T.

![NOT, AND and OR.](images/not-and-or.png){width=92%}

{{< sim file="sims/logic-lab.html" poster="sims/logic-lab.png" title="Logic Lab: NOT, AND, OR, XOR and IF–THEN" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
OR is also true when both are true.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Four cases"}
In **Logic Lab**, try the four cases of p and q. Write ¬p, p ∧ q and p ∨ q
for each.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · NOT, AND, OR"}
p = "has the key", q = "holds a torch". Choose the value.

::: {.match extra="true or false|both"}
p = T, q = F. What is p ∧ q?
:   false

p = T, q = F. What is p ∨ q?
:   true

q = F. What is ¬q?
:   true

p = F, q = F. What is p ∨ q?
:   false
:::
:::

## 16.3 XOR: exactly one

- **p ⊕ q** (XOR): true when **exactly one** is true.
- Both true or both false: false.
- In C#: `p ^ q` or `p != q`.
- The lever: left up, right down → T; both up → F.

![XOR and IF–THEN.](images/xor-implies.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"A sword or a shield, not both" is XOR, not OR.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · OR or XOR?"}
(a) attack with a sword or a bow, one at a time; (b) the alarm rings when a
door or a window opens; (c) the light is on when one switch is up.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · XOR"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="p && q|p || q"}
p = T, q = T. What is p ⊕ q?
:   false

p = F, q = T. What is p ⊕ q?
:   true

How do you write XOR for bools in C#?
:   p ^ q

"The alarm rings when a door or a window opens." Which operator?
:   OR
:::
:::

## 16.4 IF–THEN: implication

- **p → q** is false **only** when p is true and q is false.
- p → q has the same value as **¬p ∨ q**.
- Rule "crown → boss defeated" is broken only by a crown with the boss
  alive: `hasCrown && !bossDead`.
- Turning it round (q → p) is a different rule.

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
When p is false, p → q is true: the rule says nothing then.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · When is the rule broken?"}
Rule: "If the level is finished, then all coins are collected." Write the
case that breaks it, and the C# condition.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · IF–THEN"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="p && q|p is false"}
When is p → q false?
:   p is true and q is false

p = F, q = F. What is p → q?
:   true

Which expression has the same value as p → q?
:   ¬p ∨ q

Which C# condition finds a crown taken too early?
:   hasCrown && !bossDead
:::
:::

## 16.5 Compound propositions and brackets

- Order: **NOT**, then **AND**, then **OR**. Brackets first.
- p ∧ q ∨ r means (p ∧ q) ∨ r.
- Boss alive, no key, torch: b ∧ (k ∨ t) = F, but b ∧ k ∨ t = T (a bug).
- Write brackets whenever AND and OR meet.

![With and without brackets.](images/precedence.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
¬p ∧ q is (¬p) ∧ q, not ¬(p ∧ q).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Compute"}
p = T, q = F, r = T. Compute p ∨ q ∧ r, (p ∨ q) ∧ r and ¬p ∨ ¬q.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Brackets"}
p = T, q = F, r = T. Choose the value.

::: {.match extra="first OR|both"}
p ∨ q ∧ r
:   true

(p ∨ q) ∧ r
:   true

¬p ∨ ¬q
:   true

¬(p ∨ r)
:   false

What is computed first: AND or OR?
:   AND
:::
:::

## 16.6 Logic in game code

- `!` NOT, `&&` AND, `||` OR, `^` XOR.
- `&&` and `||` **stop early**: false && … is false; true || … is true.
- `enemy != null && enemy.isAlive` is safe: with no enemy, `isAlive` is
  never read.

![The condition of an if.](images/logic-code.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Single `&` and `|` never stop early; use `&&` and `||`.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Write the conditions"}
Write C# for: (a) "jump when on the ground and not stunned"; (b) "warn when
the health is below 20 or the time is below 10 seconds".
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Code"}
Choose the right condition.

::: {.match extra="onGround || !stunned|health < 20 && time < 10"}
Jump when on the ground and not stunned.
:   onGround && !stunned

Warn when the health is below 20 or the time is below 10 s.
:   health < 20 || time < 10

The shop is open in the day when the player is not in a fight.
:   isDay && !inFight

Attack only a living enemy that exists.
:   enemy != null && enemy.isAlive
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Door Logic {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

In **Torch Hall**, every door has a rule in words: the iron door, the wooden
door, a trap, a lever with two switches, the crown rule and the last gate.
Choose the condition the code must check.

{{< sim file="sims/door-logic.html" poster="sims/door-logic.png" title="Door Logic: the condition for each door" kind="game" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The doors"}
Choose the right condition.

::: {.match extra="hasKey ^ hasTorch|!hasKey"}
The iron door: the key and a torch.
:   hasKey && hasTorch

The wooden door: the key or a torch.
:   hasKey || hasTorch

The trap: no torch.
:   !hasTorch

The lever: exactly one switch up.
:   left ^ right
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 8 · The last gate (harder)"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="bossDead && hasKey || hasTorch|true"}
Which condition opens the last gate (boss defeated, and key or torch)?
:   bossDead && (hasKey || hasTorch)

Which condition checks that the crown rule is kept?
:   !hasCrown || bossDead

Boss alive, no key, torch: what is bossDead && hasKey || hasTorch?
:   true, a bug

Boss alive, no key, torch: what is bossDead && (hasKey || hasTorch)?
:   false
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- A proposition is true or false; in code it is a bool.
- NOT turns the value round; AND needs both; OR needs at least one; XOR
  needs exactly one.
- p → q is false only when p is true and q is false; it equals ¬p ∨ q.
- NOT, then AND, then OR; write brackets when AND and OR meet.
- `&&` and `||` stop early: put the safety check first.
